entries.title: Deuteronomy 24:1
segments:
vv 1-4. 
 
  Send her out of his house; this was not a command, and it was a practice contrary to the original institution of marriage.  God always abhorred it.  But on account of the wickedness and hardness of their hearts it was for a time suffered, and regulations were adopted to lessen its evils.

God, as civil ruler among the Jews, suffered, and in his providential government he now suffers some things which are contrary to his moral law, which it is wicked for men to do, and which, if they do, will draw down upon them his curse.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 24:5
segments:
Free a home one year; this was suited to increase and render more permanent conjugal affection, and thus render the family state more useful and happy. 
 
Great care should be taken not to interrupt or weaken affection between man and wife, but it should by all proper means be cherished and perpetuated.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 24:6
segments:
Nether; lower. 
 
  A man's life; that which was needful to prepare his food, and thus enable him to live.  Each family then had a mill in their house, and ground their grain by hand.
Nothing should be taken from a poor man for debt which is needful to his subsistence.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 24:7
segments: That thief shall die; he that stole an ox was to restore double, but he that stole a man was to die; so much more wicked was it to steal a man than an ox.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 24:10
segments: Not go into his house; this was designed to protect the poor debtor against the violence of the creditor.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 24:12
segments: Not sleep with his pledge; it might be some covering which at night the poor man would need.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 24:13
segments: It shall be righteousness; doing what would be right; and when done with right motives, accepted of God.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 24:15
segments:
At his day; at the close of his day's service, or the time he had agreed to work. 
 
The oppression of the poor, and withholding from hired laborers what is due to them, is an aggravated offence not only against them, but against God.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 24:16
segments:
Every man; who commits crimes for which death is the prescribed penalty. 
 
No criminal should be punished except for his own sins.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 24:18
segments:
Do this thing; refrain from wronging the laborer, the stranger, the widow, or the fatherless. 
 
The kindness of God to us should lead us to be kind to others, especially to the poor, the stranger, the widow, and the fatherless.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 24:20
segments: It; what is left on the trees.
